scope: Unpublished fragment identifier RENAME added to the existing independent definition editor. Nine authoring domains remain; no new release, commit, installation, device or execution backend protocol acceptance.
behavior: Rename changes the selected raw fragmentId value and all matching placement fragmentId reference values atomically, for placed or unused definitions.
Existing instance/group UUIDs, actor/group local keys, declaration order, effective fields, offsets and overrides remain unchanged; no UUID is generated and proposal targets is exactly [].

The new independent optional rename probe/dispatcher does not grant the old three-action capability. Missing or unsupported rename capability disables only rename; prior ADD/COPY/unplaced REMOVE and read-only locations remain available.

The form pre-fills the current ID, requires a distinct unique case-sensitive local ID, reviews every actual related placement identity, and declines unchanged IDs before requesting candidate approval.

Complete original/candidate recipes and source locations are verified within existing budgets. Declared identity/reference token replacement preserves unrelated source bytes, BOM, CRLF and original numeric spelling.

Private source ownership, raw signature, asynchronous candidate cleanup and exact completion receipt remain mandatory. Application is memory-only; ordinary Save owns persistence and external-file conflict protection.
Unused definitions retain basic registered dependency checks; first placement retains effective projection and actual image-content checks. No unplaced rendering guarantee is added.

runtime.scope: Declared sidecar archive and license prepared separately to avoid concurrent core builds. Final actual desktop resource preparation is separately recorded; no installed application acceptance.

application.sourceScope: Product and unit-test owners froze their files before this application run; these hashes still match. Only the NEW non-unit browser fixture was subsequently corrected and separately passed the final real-browser proof.

browser.savedRead409Scope: Two background saved-preview reads raced ordinary Save/rebuild; neither carried a draft. These are accounted separately from semantic candidate rejections.

screenshots.finding: No horizontal clipping or overlapping action controls. Long stable UUID references wrap within the dialog; scrolling exposes the complete raw declaration and source review.

browser.keyboardScope: Native CDP pointer opens/checks and real Escape; accepted=false then true. Snapshot input filling and delivery fault injection are intentionally explicit test instrumentation.
flowAssertions: Same-ID no-op, collisions and invalid local identifiers cannot approve or submit a preview and preserve authored input. A valid reviewed rename can be retained by declining Escape discard or canceled by accepting it, without changing any author file.

Used definition rename changes only its identity value and both source-ordered placement reference values. Stable UUID maps, original spans, BOM/CRLF, escaped key/value lexemes, exponents, offsets/overrides, four effective actors and ordered organization remain intact across three 390px languages and ordinary memory Apply/Save/reopen; silent unreviewed intent cannot apply.

After rename the existing shared-actor and organization editors still make real independently reviewed edits and ordinary saves against the new definition identity; local overrides remain authoritative. Existing placement COPY can review the renamed raw definition and cancel without applying new instances.

An unused definition rename has no generated targets and does not consume its inherited image. Its later first placement resolves real projection/image dependencies and allocates only the required stable actor/group/placement UUIDs, retaining the four earlier actors; ordinary Save/reopen keeps the renamed reference.

Rename remains available without creating declarations at the 32-fragment and 128-declared-actor limits, and can rename the only used fragment. Each real candidate retains model/counts and all fixture files stay byte-identical after cancel.

Six genuine candidate deliveries with old actor/group fragment provenance, wrong effective position/order, stale pre-rename UTF16 ranges or reordered contributors cannot approve. Detached pre-injection HTTP captures remain valid, each rejected previewId is released and the intent can be rechecked.
A real late rename response after child/parent close and a visible source edit cannot change the new owner, reopen the dialog or approve; its temporary preview is released.

When only the new rename ABI is absent or unsupported, Rename alone fails closed while original ADD/COPY/REMOVE each still perform real complete candidate checks and cancel; the existing definition CST locator remains available.

Ordinary Save conflict retains the reviewed local rename and external disk source separately. Original OC/projections/images/metadata, all limit fixtures and registry records remain unchanged; this authoring workflow never launches a backend execution job.

prepared.scope: Actual desktop/mobile copied ESM/WASM in standard VM without Node/DOM/network globals or host imports; portability only, not installation/device acceptance.

retainedAttempts.result: Initial compile failed because the new module passed tuple edits to the existing Edit struct API. New module corrected to reuse the exact shared Edit type; no existing helper changed.

retainedAttempts.reason: The initial lexical preservation test expected a global textual replacement, incorrectly changing same-named group keys and memberships. Actual core preserved those fields; new test now builds the expected result using only identity value source ranges. No product change was required.
Initial bridge suite already passed; final log repeats the frozen source.

retainedAttempts.result: Only the NEW translation fixture matched the suffix of crypto.subtle.digest as t(), incorrectly treating SHA-256 as a translatable key. Its regex now requires a word boundary. Product and old tests were unchanged.

The initial native helper build ran before the declared Node sidecar was ready and failed. Final native helper receipts verify the later successful retry; no authoring product repair is inferred from this preparation ordering failure.

The second native helper build failed because desktop/resources was not yet prepared. Final native helper receipts verify the later successful retry; the successful native-tools-build.log is not mislabeled as this initial failure.

The NEW smoke opened dialogs without trusted user activation, so Escape closed both close-watcher group members despite declining discard. This actual trace is retained; later complete trusted pointer interaction establishes the normal user behavior. No product repair was made.

The NEW smoke opened the child with a real pointer but still checked it synthetically. Escape closed the child while leaving the parent open. It still lacked the subsequent user activation needed for a cancelable close watcher; no product repair was made.

The NEW trace captured trusted cancel with cancelable:false and defaultPrevented:false before and after the existing preventDefault handler. This confirms the missing activation of the synthetic Check path; the later real-pointer Check made cancel cancelable and declining discard retained approval. No product repair was made.

With real pointer opening and Check, Escape discard decline retained the dialog and approval and accepting discard closed it. Five actual workflows passed before an unrelated NEW smoke setup evaluated multiple statements without an IIFE and failed with SyntaxError. Only that NEW fixture was corrected; product bytes remain unchanged.
The prepared proof correctly rejected a copied engine README that had become stale. Resources were refreshed from the final source; no copy mismatch is counted as a successful prepared proof.

The second prepared proof correctly rejected a NEW browser smoke file that changed after the source freeze. Its source receipt is refreshed for the final proof; no product or old-fixture workaround is implied.
The first read-only current-document review requested three scope/button-label corrections; its original report bytes are retained separately from the final recheck.

limits: Existing 128 KiB, 32 fragment definitions, 128 aggregate declared/expanded actor and group budgets.
No declaration reordering, cascading delete, spatial transformation, nested/cross-file reuse, multi-file transaction or cross-view history.
No new author resource acceptance, execution backend protocol, installed desktop build or Android device acceptance.
